en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Seventeenth Chapter
Excluding the Noble Path, are all remaining conditioned phenomena suffering? Yes.
Is the origin of suffering also suffering?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the origin of suffering also suffering?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there only three Noble Truths?
You should not speak thus …pe…
"Are there only three noble truths?
"Yes.
"But were not four noble truths taught by the Blessed One?"
"Suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice leading to the cessation of suffering"?
"Yes.
If it is true that the four noble truths were taught by the Blessed One—
There is suffering, the origin of suffering, the cessation of suffering, and the practice leading to the cessation of suffering;
surely, it should not be said that there are only three noble truths.
Is the origin of suffering also suffering?
Yes. In what sense?
In the sense of impermanence.
Is the Noble Path impermanent? Yes.
Is the Noble Path suffering?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the Noble Path impermanent, yet it is not suffering?
“Yes,” [you say].
“The origin of suffering is impermanent, yet it is not suffering”?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is the origin of suffering impermanent, and is it also suffering? Yes.
Is the noble path impermanent, and is it also suffering?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“With the exception of the Noble Path, all remaining conditioned phenomena are suffering”?
“Yes.
“Is it not the practice leading to the cessation of suffering?
“Yes.”
If that is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering, then indeed it must be said:
"With the exception of the Noble Path, all remaining conditioned phenomena are suffering.
The discussion on excluding the Noble Path is finished.
